### A Witness to the Decapolis
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/witness-decapolis
Passage: Mark 5:18-20
Points:
- An encounter with Christ leads people either to flee from His presence or to desire to remain near Him.
- Although the healed man longed to stay with Jesus, Christ denied the request in order to give him a mission.
- Sent back to his home region, the former outcast became an evangelist proclaiming God's mercy across the Decapolis.
- Believers live in the tension of longing to be with Christ while being called to serve Him in the world.
- Proclaiming God's grace to others is the believer's primary way of expressing gratitude for salvation.

### Day 152: Luke 8:26–39
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-152-luke-8-2639.html
Passage: Luke 8:26-39
Points:
- Christ's authority reigns everywhere, and demonic forces instantly recognize and submit to His supremacy.
- The powers of darkness know their time is short and an appointed reckoning awaits them.
- Solitary places can be used by God for rest, but isolation can also be exploited by the enemy.
- While fearful townspeople urged Jesus to leave, the delivered man was restored to dignity and soundness of mind.
- Rather than taking him along, Jesus sent the man home to tell his community what God had done.

### 3 Applicable Lessons from the Story of the Demon-Possessed Man
Author: Denise Kohlmeyer
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/faith/bible-study/3-applicable-lessons-from-the-story-of-the-demon-possessed-man.html
Passage: Mark 5:1-20
Points:
- No person is too broken, afflicted, or isolated to be reached and restored by the love of Jesus.
- Experiencing true spiritual deliverance produces a wholehearted desire to follow and serve Christ.
- Discipleship moves from receiving grace to going out and witnessing to friends and family first.
- A transformed life and an honest personal testimony are powerful tools for pointing others to God.
